name: Isidore Ducasse, comte de Lautréamont
credit: Alleged photograph of Isidore Ducasse (before 1870), first published in Jacques Lefrère, Le Visage de Lautréamont (1977) · Public domain (Wikimedia Commons). Text from French Wikisource (fr.wikisource.org), CC BY-SA transcription; the text is in the public domain.
bio: Isidore Ducasse was born in Montevideo, Uruguay, on 4 April 1846, the son of a French consular official. He came to France as a teenager, studied at the lycées of Tarbes and Pau, and settled in Paris about 1867. Writing under the pseudonym comte de Lautréamont, borrowed from a novel by Eugène Sue, he published the first canto of his prose epic anonymously in 1868. He died in Paris on 24 November 1870, aged twenty-four, during the siege of the city.

Les Chants de Maldoror, issued in full in 1869 (the Brussels edition was not put on sale until 1874), is a long, savage prose poem in six cantos, whose hero, Maldoror, wages a blasphemous war on God and humanity. Almost unread in his lifetime, it was rediscovered in the 1890s and was acclaimed by the Surrealists, who took it, together with his Poésies of 1870, as a founding text of their movement.
